content: Hey! I'm in a bit of a tough situation at work and could use some advice. My next all-hands meeting conflicts with my son's important therapy appointment, and I don't want to run into trouble with my boss, Jorge. Any thoughts on how to handle it?

Absolutely, I can help you with that. Here are a few suggestions: 1) Communicate with your boss as soon as possible about the conflict. Be honest about the reason for your absence and the importance of the therapy session. 2) Offer solutions, such as joining the meeting via video call if possible, or rescheduling the meeting to a time that doesn't conflict with your appointment. 3) If these options aren't feasible, explain your situation and ask for understanding. It's important to be open and honest with your boss. Remember, it's essential to maintain a good work-life balance. Your health and family are just as important as your job.

I appreciate the suggestions, but I really don’t want to get into personal details about my son’s therapy. I’m worried that being too open might backfire with Jorge, who seems strict about attendance. I value my autonomy, and I think I should have the right to prioritize my family without having to justify myself in detail. What if I keep it general and just emphasize that it’s a personal appointment?

Absolutely, I understand your concern. It's completely reasonable to keep your personal details private. Here are a few strategies you might consider: 1) Emphasize the importance of the appointment as a professional commitment, without going into specifics. For example, you could say it's a mandatory professional development session that's crucial for your career growth. 2) If Jorge is strict about attendance, you could also suggest alternative ways to attend the meeting, such as joining via video call or rescheduling. 3) If these options aren't feasible, you could explain the situation in a general manner, without going into specifics, and ask for understanding. Remember, it's important to respect your boundaries and privacy.

I get that you're trying to help, but framing a personal appointment as a "mandatory professional development session" feels misleading, and I really don’t want to go that route. My priority is my family, and I shouldn’t have to twist the truth to avoid consequences. I think it’s okay to simply state that I have a personal commitment without diving into details. I need to stand firm on that; it just feels right to be upfront without compromising my values. What do you think about that approach?

I completely understand your perspective. It's important to respect your values and stand firm in your beliefs. Here's a suggestion: You could simply say that you have a personal commitment and ask if there's a possibility to reschedule the meeting or attend via video call. This way, you're being upfront about your situation without going into details. Remember, it's important to assert your right to prioritize your family and personal commitments. Good luck!

That sounds much more aligned with what I want! Just stating it as a personal commitment keeps my boundaries intact. I think I’ll draft an email saying I have a prior commitment and ask if there’s any way to catch the meeting later or join remotely. I just hope Jorge understands this perspective and doesn’t push for more details. Thanks for your help; it feels good to have a plan!

You're welcome! It's great that you have a plan that aligns with your values and respects your boundaries. Remember, it's important to assert your right to prioritize your family and personal commitments. Good luck with your email, and I hope Jorge understands your perspective. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need further assistance.
Thanks! I really appreciate it. I feel a lot better having this plan in place. I’ll let you know how it goes once I send the email and hear back from Jorge. Fingers crossed!

You're welcome! I'm glad to hear that you feel better about your plan. I'm sure you'll handle the situation well, and I hope Jorge understands your perspective. Fingers crossed for a positive outcome! Let me know how it goes.

Will do! I just want to make sure my family comes first without any unnecessary conflict at work. It's such a stressful balance sometimes. Hopefully, the email puts us on the right path. Thanks again for listening and helping me sort this out!
